questions.title: Two Sum: Array Bounds & Duplicate Index Fix
questions.description:
Given an array of integers `nums` and an integer `target`, return the **0-based indices** of the two numbers such that they add up to `target`.

Each input has exactly one solution, and you may not use the same element twice.
Input format: First line contains integer `N`, second line contains `N` space-separated integers, third line contains integer `target`.
Output format: Print the two 0-based indices separated by a space in ascending order.

### The Bug in Starter Code:
The provided starter code suffers from an off-by-one boundary error in the inner loop and accidentally compares the same index with itself. Fix the logic to return the correct indices.
questions.inputFormat:
Line 1: N (array length)
Line 2: N space-separated integers
Line 3: target integer
questions.outputFormat: Two space-separated indices: i j (i < j)

testCases.explanation: nums[1] + nums[2] == 2 + 4 == 6. Indices are 1 2 (cannot use 0 twice).

questions.title: String Inversion with Case Flipping
questions.description:
Given a single line string `S`, reverse the entire string while **inverting the case** of every alphabetical character (lowercase becomes UPPERCASE, and UPPERCASE becomes lowercase). Non-alphabetical characters (digits, symbols, punctuation) remain unchanged.

Input format: A single line string `S`.
Output format: The reversed string with inverted letter cases.

### The Bug in Starter Code:
The starter code reverses the string but omits the case inversion for lowercase letters and crashes on spaces. Fix it so all tests pass.
questions.outputFormat: Reversed string with inverted letter case
constraints: S may contain letters, digits, punctuation, and spaces.

testCases.explanation: Reversed is "dlroWolleH", with inverted case is "DLROwOLLEh".
Reversed order, letters case swapped, spaces and numbers unchanged.

questions.title: Binary Search: Midpoint Overflow & Loop Condition
questions.description:
Given a sorted array of `N` integers in non-decreasing order and a query value `X`, find the **first (leftmost) 0-based index** where `nums[i] >= X`.
If all elements are smaller than `X`, output `N`.

Input format:
Line 1: `N` (number of elements)
Line 2: `N` space-separated sorted integers
Line 3: `Q` (number of queries)
Line 4: `Q` space-separated integers representing query values `X`

Output format:
Print `Q` space-separated indices.
questions.inputFormat:
N
N sorted integers
Q
Q query integers

starterCode.python:
import sys

def lower_bound(nums, x):
    low = 0
    high = len(nums) - 1
    ans = len(nums)

    while low < high: # BUG: misses low == high case
        mid = (low + high) // 2
        if nums[mid] >= x:
            ans = mid
            high = mid - 1
        else:
            low = mid + 1
    return ans

def solve():
    data = sys.stdin.read().split()
    if not data:
        return
    n = int(data[0])
    nums = [int(x) for x in data[1:n+1]]
    q = int(data[n+1])
    queries = [int(x) for x in data[n+2:n+2+q]]

    results = [str(lower_bound(nums, q_val)) for q_val in queries]
    print(" ".join(results))

if __name__ == '__main__':
    solve()

solutionCode.python:
import sys
import bisect

def solve():
    data = sys.stdin.read().split()
    if not data:
        return
    n = int(data[0])
    nums = [int(x) for x in data[1:n+1]]
    q = int(data[n+1])
    queries = [int(x) for x in data[n+2:n+2+q]]

    results = [str(bisect.bisect_left(nums, x)) for x in queries]
    print(" ".join(results))

if __name__ == '__main__':
    solve()

questions.title: Syntax Validator: Balanced Nested Delimiters
questions.description: Given a string containing only brackets `()`, `{}`, `[]`, determine if the input string is valid.
questions.inputFormat:
T
T lines of bracket strings

starterCode.java:
import java.util.*;
public class Solution { static boolean isValid(String s) { Deque<Character> stack = new ArrayDeque<>(); for (char c : s.toCharArray()) { if (c == '(' || c == '{' || c == '[') stack.push(c); else { char top = stack.pop(); if ((c == ')' && top != '(') || (c == '}' && top != '{') || (c == ']' && top != '[')) return false; } } return true; } public static void main(String[] args) { Scanner sc = new Scanner(System.in); if (!sc.hasNextInt()) return; int t = sc.nextInt(); while (t-- > 0) { System.out.println(isValid(sc.next()) ? "VALID" : "INVALID"); } } }

questions.title: Longest Palindromic Span Debugger
questions.description: Given a string `S`, return the length of the longest palindromic contiguous substring in `S`.
constraints: S consists of lowercase English letters only.

starterCode.python:
import sys
def solve():
    s = sys.stdin.read().strip()
    if not s:
        print(0)
        return
    n = len(s)
    max_len = 1
    for i in range(n):
        l, r = i, i
        while l >= 0 and r < n and s[l] == s[r]:
            max_len = max(max_len, r - l + 1)
            l -= 1
            r += 1
    print(max_len)
if __name__ == '__main__':
    solve()
starterCode.java:
import java.util.*;
public class Solution { public static void main(String[] args) { Scanner sc = new Scanner(System.in); if (!sc.hasNext()) return; String s = sc.next(); int n = s.length(), maxLen = 1; for (int i = 0; i < n; i++) { int l = i, r = i; while (l >= 0 && r < n && s.charAt(l) == s.charAt(r)) { maxLen = Math.max(maxLen, r - l + 1); l--; r++; } } System.out.println(maxLen); } }

questions.title: Prime Factorization & GCD Accelerator
questions.description: Given two positive 64-bit integers `A` and `B`, find the **Greatest Common Divisor (GCD)** of `A` and `B`, and print the **sum of distinct prime factors** of that GCD.

starterCode.python:
import sys, math
def sum_distinct_primes(n):
    if n <= 1: return 0
    total = 0
    d = 2
    while d * d <= n:
        if n % d == 0:
            total += d
            while n % d == 0: n //= d
        d += 1
    return total
def solve():
    d = sys.stdin.read().split()
    if len(d) < 2: return
    a, b = int(d[0]), int(d[1])
    g = math.gcd(a, b)
    print(f"{g} {sum_distinct_primes(g)}")
if __name__ == '__main__': solve()
starterCode.java:
import java.util.*;
public class Solution { static long gcd(long a, long b) { while (b != 0) { long t = b; b = a % b; a = t; } return a; } static long sumDistinctPrimes(long n) { if (n <= 1) return 0; long total = 0; for (long d = 2; d * d <= n; d++) { if (n % d == 0) { total += d; while (n % d == 0) n /= d; } } return total; } public static void main(String[] args) { Scanner sc = new Scanner(System.in); if (!sc.hasNextLong()) return; long a = sc.nextLong(), b = sc.nextLong(); long g = gcd(a, b); System.out.println(g + " " + sumDistinctPrimes(g)); } }

solutionCode.python:
import sys, math
def solve():
    d = sys.stdin.read().split()
    if len(d) < 2: return
    a, b = int(d[0]), int(d[1])
    g = math.gcd(a, b)
    if g <= 1: print(f"{g} 0"); return
    n, total, d = g, 0, 2
    while d * d <= n:
        if n % d == 0:
            total += d
            while n % d == 0: n //= d
        d += 1
    if n > 1: total += n
    print(f"{g} {total}")
if __name__ == '__main__': solve()
